caustica.options.rt.offlineDenoise.toolt: Off by default. Uses measured sample variation to reduce uncertain bright points and grain; stable details are retained. Requires at least 32 accumulated frames. Rare highlights may still be misclassified. Toggle compares against unchanged raw accumulation without resetting samples. Source view only. The rejected 0.3.16 filter setting is not inherited.
caustica.options.rt.offlineRegularizatio: Experimental; active only during offline accumulation. Reduces some indirect reflection noise while preserving the visible surface's authored roughness. May change indirect highlights, caustics and brightness. Does not regularize water or glass interfaces. Changing this resets accumulation; Off retains the original result.
caustica.options.rt.offlineRendering.too: After the camera is still, freezes single-player game ticks and progressively accumulates native-resolution path tracing. Temporarily bypasses DLSS Ray Reconstruction and Frame Generation. Multiplayer servers require /tick freeze. Moving the camera resets accumulated samples.
caustica.options.rt.exposureMode.tooltip: How the ray-traced image is mapped to display brightness. Auto adapts to scene luminance; Manual uses the exposure value directly.
caustica.options.rt.manualEv.tooltip: Exposure compensation in stops. In Manual, this is the fixed exposure. In Auto, this biases the auto exposure brighter or darker.
caustica.options.rt.spp.tooltip: Path-tracing samples taken per pixel each frame. In offline rendering this is only the per-frame batch size; quality follows total samples accumulated, so a smaller batch can update the display faster.
caustica.options.rt.maxBounces.tooltip: Maximum number of secondary path-tracing bounces after the primary hit. Higher captures more indirect light but costs more.
caustica.options.rt.offlineMaxBounces.to: Path-bounce limit used only while Offline Rendering is accumulating. Higher values capture more indirect light but greatly increase render time.
caustica.options.rt.sunSize.tooltip: Angular radius of the sun and moon disk. Larger discs cast softer shadow penumbrae.
caustica.options.rt.entities.tooltip: Include entities and block entities in the ray-traced scene.
caustica.options.rt.particles.tooltip: Draw particles as camera-ray billboards inside the traced scene.
caustica.options.rt.glow.tooltip: Draw the vanilla Glowing-effect outline (through walls) around glowing entities.
caustica.options.rt.waterWaves.tooltip: Animate water-surface normals for moving wave highlights.
caustica.options.rt.hdr.tooltip: Present in HDR (ST.2084/PQ) instead of SDR, when the display supports it. Takes effect after restarting the game.
caustica.options.rt.hdrPaperWhite.toolti: Absolute brightness (in nits) that SDR-equivalent scene brightness maps to on an HDR display.
caustica.options.rt.hdrPeak.tooltip: Absolute brightness (in nits) highlights roll off toward. Set to your display's peak HDR brightness.
caustica.options.rt.dlssQuality.tooltip: DLSS Ray Reconstruction quality mode. Lower-quality modes render fewer pixels and upscale more aggressively for higher framerates; higher-quality modes render more pixels for a sharper image. Only affects the image when DLSS Ray Reconstruction is enabled.
caustica.options.rt.frameGeneration.tool: Inserts one generated frame between rendered frames (2x). Requires a supported NVIDIA RTX GPU and driver. Higher multipliers are not exposed because they are currently unstable. Cannot be used with Offline Rendering.
caustica.options.rt.debugView.tooltip: Views 1-7 show guide buffers. Offline contribution views 8-21 apply only while accumulating; movement shows the normal image. Use fixed manual exposure for comparisons. Views 8-11 include all path depths; view 12 selects bounce > 0, not a complete physical indirect-light decomposition.
